name: CH-46 Sea Knight / Boeing Vertol 107
summary: A tandem-rotor transport helicopter, retired by the Marine Corps and still flown by commercial heavy-lift operators as the Vertol 107.

wings: Two three-blade rotors in tandem, one forward and one raised aft
Rotors overlap little; no tail rotor needed
engines: Two turboshafts in pods on either side of the aft pylon
Exhausts at the rear of each engine
fuselage: Long rounded fuselage with a rear loading ramp
Short stub sponsons holding the fixed main wheels
Row of windows and a cabin door on the right side
tail: Aft rotor pylon rises on the tail with a vertical fin

tellTales: Two rotors in tandem, front and rear
Rear loading ramp on a rounded fuselage
Engines at the base of the tall aft pylon

confusedWith.howToTell: The Chinook is larger and boxier with full-length fuel sponsons; the CH-46 is smaller with stub sponsons and a rounder body.
The Osprey has tilting rotors on wing tips; the CH-46 has two rotors on pylons with no wings.

usCount.source: FAA Releasable Aircraft Database — valid registrations
